chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, and from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man leaves his father or his mother or his son or his daughter, if he leaves one of these four, then they are not those meant by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He said: 'Say: Allah gives you a verdict concerning the Kalala.'

key_terms.الْكَلالَةِ: Kalala (a person who has neither parents nor children)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Kalala in Islamic inheritance law according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the term 'Kalala' in Quran 4:176 specifically excludes those who leave behind direct ascendants (parents) or descendants (sons/daughters), thereby refining the legal scope of inheritance distribution. This hadith is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between primary heirs and the residual 'Kalala' category, ensuring that the presence of even one direct lineal relative precludes the application of the Kalala inheritance rules.
